chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'In the house of singing (music), one is not safe from calamity, nor are supplications answered therein, nor do the angels enter it.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual consequences of having singing or music in the house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical impact of *ghina* (melodic singing) on the domestic sphere, asserting that such environments repel angels and hinder the acceptance of supplications. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between permissible recitation and distracting musical entertainment, emphasizing the preservation of spiritual purity within the home.
